title: The Intimacy of God's Omniscience
speaker: Mr. Alex Lyro
series: Anxiety and the Character of God

outline.title: Reviewing the Nature of Anxiety
subpoints: Anxiety is an issue of the inner man and heart orientation
It is a daily battle of interpretation requiring trust in God's plan
Recognizing anxiety as sin points us to Christ for repentance

outline.title: Reframing God's Omniscience
subpoints: Moving beyond the 'Three O's' emphasis on behavioral compliance
Shifting focus from fear of being watched to comfort in being known
Understanding omniscience as a source of praise and intimacy

outline.title: The Immensity of God's Knowledge
subpoints: God's knowledge is exhaustive, static, and not derived from learning
He knows all stars, nations, and creatures with perfect clarity
Examples include the naming of stars and the tracking of animal populations

outline.title: The Intimacy of God's Knowledge (Psalm 139)
subpoints: God knows the individual personally, not just generally
He understands thoughts, paths, and hidden struggles
His knowledge is a source of comfort against feelings of isolation

outline.title: God Knows You Personally
subpoints: The verb 'searched' implies deep investigation of the heart
God knows fears, temperaments, and unarticulated burdens
His love persists despite His complete knowledge of human weakness

outline.title: God Knows Your Actions
subpoints: He is aware of ordinary daily movements and routines
He oversees daily providences, deadlines, and unseen faithfulness
His knowledge extends to the mundane details that cause worry

summary: This lesson continues a series on addressing anxiety through the character of God, specifically focusing on the doctrine of divine omniscience. The speaker begins by reviewing previous points, establishing that anxiety is fundamentally an issue of the heart's orientation and trust rather than external circumstances. The aim is to reframe the common childhood understanding of God's omniscience—which often emphasizes surveillance and behavioral compliance—into a mature appreciation of God's intimate knowledge as a source of comfort.
